title: Chapter 4 Assessment: Record Data Types, Subroutines and Logic Circuits
instructions: Answer all questions. Write pseudocode in Cambridge style. Use RECORD … ENDRECORD for record types. Calculators are not permitted.

questions.text: Which **data type** would be most suitable for storing the price of an item in a shop database?

options.text: INTEGER
REAL
STRING
BOOLEAN

questions.explanation: Money has a fractional part (e.g. 4.99), so a REAL is needed. A STRING keeps the digits but cannot be used in calculations.

options.text: A collection of items of the same data type stored under one identifier
A collection of related data items that may have different data types, stored under one identifier
A single value that can only be TRUE or FALSE
A value stored in a text file

questions.explanation: A record groups fields of mixed types (e.g. StudentID: INTEGER, Name: STRING). Option A describes an array.

questions.text:
A school stores data about students in a record. Each student has a 4-digit ID, a name, a date of birth and whether they are a boarder.

Write pseudocode to **define the record type** `Student` and **declare** one variable `newStudent` of this type.

answer.text: TYPE Student
DECLARE StudentID : INTEGER (or STRING) / DECLARE Name : STRING
DECLARE DateOfBirth : DATE / DECLARE IsBoarder : BOOLEAN
ENDTYPE then DECLARE newStudent : Student

questions.explanation:
Cambridge form:

TYPE Student
    DECLARE StudentID : INTEGER
    DECLARE Name : STRING
    DECLARE DateOfBirth : DATE
    DECLARE IsBoarder : BOOLEAN
ENDTYPE
DECLARE newStudent : Student

questions.text: A **user-defined enumerated type** is BEST described as:

options.text: A list of all possible values that a variable of that type may take
A record containing several fields
An array of integers
A pointer to another variable

questions.explanation: e.g. TYPE Colour = (Red, Green, Blue) — the variable may only hold one of the listed values, which makes the code easier to read and validate.

questions.text: Which statement about **procedures** and **functions** is correct?

options.text: A function must always return a value; a procedure does not return a value
A procedure must always return a value; a function does not
Both must return exactly one value
Neither can take parameters

questions.explanation: A function is used in an expression and returns a single value via RETURN. A procedure performs a task and is called as a statement.

questions.text: Explain the difference between **passing a parameter by value** and **passing a parameter by reference**, and state which one must be used if a subroutine is to change the value of the calling variable.

answer.text: By value: a copy of the data is passed, so changes made inside the subroutine do not affect the original variable.
By reference: the address of the variable is passed, so changes made inside the subroutine modify the original variable.
By reference must be used (Cambridge pseudocode: BYREF).

questions.explanation: In Cambridge pseudocode this is written as PROCEDURE Update(BYREF Score : INTEGER) for reference and BYVAL for value.

questions.text: Write a pseudocode **function** `CalcAverage` that takes an array `Marks` of 10 integers and returns the average of the ten marks, rounded to **one decimal place**.

answer.text: Correct function header: FUNCTION CalcAverage(Marks : ARRAY[1:10] OF INTEGER) RETURNS REAL
Declares a running total and sets it to 0
Loop from 1 to 10, adding each mark to the total
Calculates total / 10 and rounds (e.g. ROUND(Total / 10, 1))
Returns the result with RETURN; ENDFUNCTION

questions.explanation:
FUNCTION CalcAverage(Marks : ARRAY[1:10] OF INTEGER) RETURNS REAL
    DECLARE Total : INTEGER
    DECLARE Index : INTEGER
    Total ← 0
    FOR Index ← 1 TO 10
        Total ← Total + Marks[Index]
    NEXT Index
    RETURN ROUND(Total / 10, 1)
ENDFUNCTION

questions.text:
Trace the procedure below when called as `Change(X)` with `X = 5`.

```
PROCEDURE Change(BYVAL N : INTEGER)
    N ← N * 2
    OUTPUT N
ENDPROCEDURE
```

Complete the trace table and state the final value of `X` in the calling program.
questions.explanation: BYVAL passes a copy, so N becomes 10 and 10 is output, but the original X stays 5. Swap in BYREF and see the difference: X would also become 10.

questions.text:
Trace the pseudocode and state the **output**.

```
DECLARE A : INTEGER
DECLARE B : INTEGER
A ← 3
B ← 4
CALL Swap(A, B)
OUTPUT A, B

PROCEDURE Swap(BYREF P : INTEGER, BYREF Q : INTEGER)
    DECLARE Temp : INTEGER
    Temp ← P
    P ← Q
    Q ← Temp
ENDPROCEDURE
```

answer.text: Recognises the parameters are passed by reference
P and Q swap: P = 4, Q = 3, and these are the same storage locations as A and B
Output: 4 3

questions.explanation: Answer = 4 3. If the header had BYVAL the output would be 3 4.

questions.text: A logic circuit's output is 1 only when **exactly one** of its two inputs is 1. Which gate is it?

options.text: AND
OR
XOR
NOR

questions.explanation: XOR (exclusive OR) gives 1 when the inputs are different: 0,1 and 1,0.

questions.text: Complete the truth table for **X = (A XOR B) AND C**.
questions.explanation: X is 1 only when A and B differ AND C is 1.

questions.text: Draw / describe a logic circuit that implements **X = (A AND B) OR (NOT C)** using AND, OR and NOT gates, and state the output when A = 1, B = 0, C = 0.

answer.text: AND gate with inputs A and B
NOT gate with input C
OR gate taking the outputs of both as inputs, producing X
When A = 1, B = 0, C = 0: (1 AND 0) OR (NOT 0) = 0 OR 1 = 1

questions.explanation: Two sub-expressions feeding one final OR gate. Always evaluate each bracket separately before combining.

questions.text:
A record type has been defined as:

```
TYPE Book
    DECLARE Title : STRING
    DECLARE Pages : INTEGER
ENDTYPE
DECLARE myBook : Book
```

Write pseudocode statements to **assign** the title "CS Basics" and the value 240 to the fields of `myBook`.

answer.text: myBook.Title ← "CS Basics"
myBook.Pages ← 240

questions.explanation: Fields are accessed with dot notation: recordName.fieldName.

questions.text: What is the main advantage of using **subroutines** in a program?

options.text: The program runs without needing variables
Code can be reused and the program is easier to test and maintain
The program will always be shorter than 100 lines
Subroutines remove the need for comments

questions.explanation: Subroutines avoid duplication (reusability), make code easier to read, debug, test and maintain — one change fixes every call.

questions.text: Write a pseudocode **procedure** `PrintDetails` that takes a `Student` record **by value** and outputs the student's name and ID on one line, then explain why passing the record by value is appropriate here.

answer.text: PROCEDURE PrintDetails(StudentRecord : Student) with correct parameter
OUTPUT StudentRecord.Name, StudentRecord.StudentID
Correct ENDPROCEDURE and use of dot notation
By value is appropriate because the procedure only reads/displays the data and must not change the original record (protects the original data).

questions.explanation: Passing a record BYVAL also prevents accidental corruption of the stored data.

questions.text:
An array `Scores` of 8 integers already contains data.

Write pseudocode to find and output the **highest** score and the **position (index)** at which it occurs.

answer.text: Initialises Highest ← Scores[1] and Position ← 1
FOR loop from 2 TO 8
IF Scores[Index] > Highest THEN updates Highest
Also updates Position ← Index inside the IF
Outputs both Highest and Position after the loop

questions.explanation:
DECLARE Highest : INTEGER
DECLARE Position : INTEGER
Highest ← Scores[1]
Position ← 1
FOR Index ← 2 TO 8
    IF Scores[Index] > Highest THEN
        Highest ← Scores[Index]
        Position ← Index
    ENDIF
NEXT Index
OUTPUT "Highest: ", Highest, " at position ", Position

questions.text: Which is a valid reason for using a **user-defined data type**?

options.text: It makes the program run faster
It makes the code self-documenting and restricts a variable to sensible values
It removes the need for validation
It reduces the size of the executable file

questions.explanation: User-defined types improve readability and make the programmer's intent clear; they can also help validation but do not replace it.

questions.text:
The following function contains an error:

```
FUNCTION GetTotal(A : INTEGER, B : INTEGER)
    DECLARE Sum : INTEGER
    Sum ← A + B
ENDFUNCTION
```

Identify the error and write the corrected line.

answer.text: The function does not return a value.
Add RETURN Sum before ENDFUNCTION.

questions.explanation: A FUNCTION must return a value; otherwise it should be written as a PROCEDURE.
